title: The New York Listing Ali Parsa Later Called His Biggest Mistake
conflicts: Share prices differ because of the December 2022 reverse split ($272.50 peak per The National and TelecareAware; almost $243 opening and over $3.5bn market value per pharmaphorum), so no share price is used, only The National's 'more than 99%' fall. 2022 losses differ ($369.8m group net loss per MedCity; 173.7m pounds per BusinessCloud, apparently a different entity), so only the agreed Q1 2023 loss of $63.2m is used. Staff: 1,895 at end 2022 (TelecareAware, from filings) versus about 1,900 global and 650 UK from LinkedIn (BusinessCloud); story uses 1,895, dated. UKTN dates the listing to June 2021 (the announcement); completion was October 2021. GP at Hand: The National says the app went with the eMed sale, TechCrunch says the practice was not part of it; story says only that it kept running.
notes: The slate's 'a year after going public' is wrong: listing October 2021, collapse August 2023 (about 22 months); the story gives the dates. Parsa made no public statement on the collapse, so his voice comes from June 2021 (tech.eu) and his own later verdicts reported by The National (FT, Nov 2022) and Bloomberg via Gulf Times (Sifted, 2022). Blame is attributed only in his own words; clinicians' allegations are not used. talQen is mentioned once, in the reflection. Guardian, BBC, Reuters, Wired, Forbes, Sifted, FT and Fierce Healthcare could not be read.
